1.he: לְרוּם גָּבַר וְעִם אֵל וֶאֱנוֹשׁ רָד
1.note: Two verses about the poet's name: Hos 12:1 "Judah yet rules with God" (עֹד רָד עִם אֵל) and Gen 32:29 "you have striven with God and with men, and prevailed" (גָּבַר). "Ruled" for רָד follows Hosea; in the rhyme of the poem רָד also means "went down", as in line 1.

2.note: ענק is a necklace. It may also point to al-Ḥarizi's book of short poems, Sefer ha-Anak ("The Necklace").

3.note: In Isa 3:20 these are women's ornaments, perfume boxes and amulets. Here the words are taken in their literal sense, "houses of the soul" and "whisperings", as things in the upper world. The exact sense is uncertain.

4.note: Lev 6:2. עוֹלָה is the burnt offering, and also "she who goes up": the soul that rises.

5.note: A pun: קִנָּהּ "her nest" and קוֹנָהּ "her Owner" (the Creator, as in Gen 14:19 קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ). The stork (חֲסִידָה) of the next line is also "the pious one".

6.note: עֶרֶץ, "awe", rhymes with אֶרֶץ, "earth". Line 161 has שְׁמֵי עֶרֶץ, "the heavens of awe", so the pair may mean "earth and the awesome heavens".

7.he: וְכִי אוֹצִיא לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִבֵּין הַמְּצָרִים
7.note: Lam 1:3 "between the straits". מְּצָרִים also sounds like מִצְרַיִם, Egypt: the Hebrew language in bondage, as Israel was.

8.he: עַד אָבַד בְּתוֹכָם וּלְשׁוֹן קֵדָר הִקְדִּירַתְהוּ
8.note: A pun: Kedar (the Arabs) and הִקְדִּיר, "made dark".

9.note: The edition points חֲתֵה as an imperative, so the maiden speaks: "Drink, and take up coals from my lips" (compare Isa 30:14 לַחְתּוֹת אֵשׁ). This changes Gen 24:14, where Rebekah says "Drink, and I will water your camels too".

10.note: The root גאל means both "redeem" (גּוֹאֵל, the line before) and "defile" (Mal 1:7). Here it is "defile".

11.note: m. Qiddushin 1:1: a woman is betrothed by money, by a deed, or by intercourse. He betroths the Hebrew language without the last two, that is, by the gifts of the line before.

12.note: רְפָאִים are both giants (Deut 2:11) and the shades of the dead (Isa 26:14, 19). The tongue fells the one and raises the other.

13.note: Cain's brother is Hevel (Abel), whose name means "vapor, vanity": the Hebrew language is held to be worth nothing.

14.note: Jer 22:14 בֵּית מִדּוֹת, "a spacious house". מִדּוֹת also means measures (the meters of poems) and virtues.

15.note: A pun: נִרְדָּם "asleep" and בְּנִרְדָּם "with their spikenard" (Song 1:12).

16.note: Isa 47:8 calls Babylon עֲדִינָה, "the voluptuous one", and line 594 has "from Egypt to Babylon", so Adina is probably Babylon (Iraq). The city of Aden is also possible.

17.note: Gen 3:7. עֲרֻמִּים is "naked", and the same letters also mean "cunning" (Gen 3:1): they will see that they lack eloquence, and they will become clever.

18.note: A rhyme pair: בָּרַחְתִּי "I fled" and זָרַחְתִּי "I shone, rose" like the sun in the East (מִזְרָח, from the same root).

19.note: The edition prints זצ"ל ("of blessed memory"), which is unusual for a living patron; it may come from a later copy. The manuscripts of the Taḥkemoni do not all have the same dedication.

20.note: A pun on the name Ezra: בְעֶזְרָם "their help". Deut 33:26 "who rides the heavens to your help" (בְעֶזְרֶךָ).
